header: Meeting header: 2026-06-14 15:00 UTC | Duration: 55 minutes | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Samir Gupta (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (OakBridge Head of Procurement), Daniel Kim (OakBridge InfoSec), Lara Nguyen (OakBridge ML Platform). Zoom. Recorded by Fireflies.
summary: Customer (OakBridge) is green-lighting a short pilot but needs clarified acceptance criteria: latency SLAs for 99th percentile, KMS/HSM integration path, data residency and egress pricing, and a redlined MSA. Redwood to supply SOC2 docs, pilot SOW, and benchmark sheet. Pricing conversation oriented around reserved capacity vs burst and whether quantization allowed under contract.
topics: Pilot SOW and acceptance criteria (latency, correctness)
KMS/HSM integration and key management options
Data residency / egress fees / region routing
SLA targets and rollback/fallback model variants
Pricing: reserved capacity vs usage, burst pricing
Benchmarks and pilot telemetry to validate cost model
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everybody, thanks for joining, uh let's do quick intros, I'm Maya Patel, AE on the OakBridge account.
[00:12] Priya (OakBridge): Priya Shah, procurement. Thanks, Maya.
[00:18] Samir (Redwood SE): Samir Gupta, solutions eng, I'll cover the pilot bench and the KMS flows.
[00:24] Daniel (OakBridge): Daniel Kim, InfoSec, quick note: we'll need HSM or equivalent and SOC two docs.
[00:30] Lara (OakBridge): Lara Nguyen, ML platform, hi. We care about tail latency and cost per call.
[00:38] Maya: Cool, agenda — MSA redline status, pilot acceptance criteria, KMS trajectory, pricing lanes. We only have 55 mins so we'll go fast.
[00:47] Priya: Quick context — legal needs to see a redline and the SOW, procurement wants committed vs burst pricing options. We have a runbook for egress costs we can share.
[00:58] Samir: Sounds good; for the pilot we recommend a 2-week run with reserved tiny capacity and a fallback to hosted when burst happens. We'll share numbers in the bench sheet.
[01:10] Daniel: On KMS: are you using customer-managed keys? Do you support Cloud HSM, AWS KMS or key-on-prem? There was confusion in the RFP — K-M-S spelled out in doc.
[01:22] Maya: Short answer: yes, Redwood Private supports customer KMS; for Hosted we provide an option to bring your own key via KMS or an HSM integrator. We'll provide the architecture diagram.
[01:33] Lara: Important — we need per-request logs and an audit trail, also the ability to rotate keys without downtime.
[01:41] Samir: Rotation pattern we use is tokenized key wrap, same pattern used by other customers. There might be a small token re-key latency, typically sub-second but we will validate.
[01:52] Priya: On MSA, legal flagged two clauses — indemnity language and an SLA escrow fallback — will you accept limited liability cap tied to monthly committed spend?
[02:05] Maya: We can propose a cap tied to committed capacity for Dedicated; for Hosted it's trickier but we have standard lanes. I'll get legal to propose language but need to see their suggested redlines.
[02:18] Daniel: Also data residency — some PII must stay in eu-west-1, will Redwood route by policy?
[02:26] Samir: Yes, routing policies exist, can pin to region; we'll document the routing rules and trace. Slightly noisy transcription: he said "pin to region" but engineer said "pinned region".
[02:38] Lara: For pilot acceptance — we want 95% requests under 120ms p50 and p99 under 450ms for the sample prompt set, and throughput to sustain 200 qps burst for 2 minutes.
[02:52] Maya: We discussed those numbers internally — our bench numbers for the curated model are p50 80-100ms, p99 ~350ms at similar seq lengths, but depends a lot on batching and quantization.
[03:06] Priya: Quantization — is it allowed under the agreement? Some compliance folks say quantization may change outputs and we need to lock the deterministic bit.
[03:17] Samir: Good point, quantization can slightly affect logits; for customer-facing features we recommend A/B evals; we'll include quality reg checks in SOW acceptance criteria.
[03:28] Daniel: On egress fees — procurement wants a predictable cap; we might commit to monthly tokens, but need clarity on how caching and prefix KV caching affects billing.
[03:39] Maya: Redwood Optimize suggestions will show estimate savings with prefix caching; we'll include modeled spend for the pilot traffic pattern.
[03:48] Lara: Can you share the telemetry we need to measure inference quality? We want per-route latency, token counts, and sample traces for regen cases.
[03:58] Samir: Yes — we'll expose per-request traces and token breakdowns. Small mention that the transcript sometimes shows "KV cache" as "city cache" — ignore that.
[04:10] Priya: Timeline — procurement can approve SOW if we get redlined MSA and SOC2 by June 18, legal meeting on June 20. Can we meet that?
[04:20] Maya: That's tight but doable; I'll push legal. Samir, can you get bench sheet out tomorrow?
[04:27] Samir: I can send a draft bench sheet by EOD tomorrow — it will include config: batch sizes, quantization options, warm-up steps, p50/p90/p99 numbers.
[04:36] Daniel: For keys — can you confirm whether Redwood keeps any plaintext model context outside the customer's tenancy? We need explicit statement.
[04:45] Maya: Short answer: no plaintext persisted outside the customer's VPC variant for Private; for Hosted we'll provide details and options for bring-your-own-key, and an option for private control plane. We'll attach the security whitepaper.
[04:58] Lara: Also want to test failover: if Dedicated capacity dips, we want automatic fallback to a compatible model variant with slightly higher latency but preserved behavior.
[05:08] Samir: We have a fallback policy feature; can be configured in rollout. We'll include suggested settings in SOW.
[05:17] Priya: Pricing ask — procurement prefers a nominal reserved commit for pilot (e.g., 1 GPU equiv) with clear burst rates. If the cost is too high, we may trial purely hosted but that affects egress cost predictability.
[05:30] Maya: We'll provide two price lanes: Reserved pilot price and Hosted pay-as-you-go price with egress estimate. Also note, quantization may reduce cost by 30-60% depending.
[05:40] Daniel: Legal also asked about audit logs retention — we need 12 months in the contract, plus exportability for audits.
[05:49] Maya: Standard is 6 months; 12 months is an enterprise add-on — we can put it in SOW as an option and price it.
[05:58] Lara: One more — we need sample payloads and representative prompt set to run bench. I'll send by end of day tomorrow.
[06:05] Priya: Recap?
[06:08] Maya: Recap: Redwood sends MSA redline, pricing lanes, SOC2 and security whitepaper; Samir sends bench spreadsheet; OakBridge to send sample prompts and KMS requirements; schedule pilot kickoff week of 6/22.
[06:22] Priya: OK thanks, that works.
[06:25] Daniel: I'll follow up with a short list of KMS questions.
[06:28] Maya: Great — we'll aim to hit the June 18 redline target. Thanks everyone.
[06:33] [meeting ends]
notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-hears (e.g., 'K-M-S' transcribed variably). Emphasis on legal redlines, KMS trajectory, and pilot acceptance metrics. Customer leans toward reserved pilot if price aligns.
